description: Recorded LLM output for offline fallback. Rule candidates extracted from the Chief Engineer onboarding transcript by the schema-constrained scribe, one per rule, each anchored to the expert turns it came from. Candidates await confirmation on the Decision Canvas.

rule_candidates.title: Water near switchgear or electrical room — evacuate and escalate
rule_candidates.decision: Treat as electrical hazard. Evacuate the electrical room immediately. Nobody enters until LEW confirms de-energised and safe. Isolate water upstream of the room outside the threshold. Call LEW and Duty Manager.
allowed_actions: Cordon and signage at electrical room threshold
Upstream water isolation outside the room
Log and photograph from outside the threshold
forbidden_actions: Entering the room before LEW confirms de-energised and safe
Operating any wet breaker or switch
Powering pumps or wet-vacs from the affected board
Security 'quick look' entry

exceptions.note: LEW confirms the affected section is a spare/dead board and documents it
Water confined to a sealed trench with no contact path — LEW judgement

rule_candidates.title: Isolate at the nearest isolation sub-valve — branch before riser
rule_candidates.decision: Isolate at the nearest accessible isolation sub-valve. For a branch leak where the sub-valve is accessible and stops the flow, isolate the branch only and leave the riser open. Isolate the riser only when the leak is on the riser pipe, the sub-valve is seized or inaccessible, or the source is not confirmed within 10 minutes. In a tenant-occupied area isolation must be complete within the deadline; if it is not, escalate to the Duty Facilities Manager.
allowed_actions: Close the riser valve (riser-pipe leak, seized sub-valve, or source unconfirmed at 10 min)
forbidden_actions: Closing any fire-protection valve without FSM authorisation (see TS-05)
Shutting the whole riser for a branch leak the sub-valve can stop
Leaving an isolated valve unlabelled

exceptions.note: Leak is on the riser pipe itself — isolate the riser
Branch sub-valve seized or inaccessible — isolate the riser
Source is behind a locked tenancy — arrange tenant access, then isolate locally

rule_candidates.distinguishing_condition: Branch leak with a working sub-valve -> isolate the branch only. Riser-pipe leak, seized/inaccessible sub-valve, or source unconfirmed at 10 min -> isolate the riser. Condensate -> AHU unit level, never the riser.

rule_candidates.title: Do not shut down whole floor power unless electrical risk confirmed
rule_candidates.decision: Do not shut down a whole floor's power based on a tenant request or a precautionary instinct. Power-down only when electrical risk is confirmed by the LEW or by clear evidence: water on switchgear, breaker already tripped, or insulation resistance below threshold. A false power-down on a bank anchor tenant's trading floor is a seven-figure incident.
allowed_actions: Send technician to assess with moisture meter
Request LEW inspection if risk uncertain
Isolate individual affected circuit on LEW advice
forbidden_actions: Shutting down a whole floor on tenant request alone
Shutting down a whole floor without LEW or confirmed evidence
De-energising circuits not in the water path

exceptions.note: Water confirmed on switchgear — TS-01 electrical gate applies
Breaker already tripped — the LEW inspects the tripped circuit before any reset or wider power-down (a reset is a re-energisation, TS-07)

rule_candidates.title: Condensate vs active leak — distinguish before committing resources
rule_candidates.decision: Determine whether this is condensate (tray overflow, drain blockage) or an active chilled-water branch leak. Condensate is a drip, ambient temperature, from the condensate tray or drain line. Active chilled-water is a stream, cold (8-14 degrees C), from the branch pipe or riser. Condensate: clear tray, place drip protection, schedule repair. Active leak: isolate the FCU chilled-water isolation valves immediately (TS-02). When in doubt, treat as active and isolate.
allowed_actions: Inspect condensate tray and drain line
Place drip tray and absorbent socks
Close FCU chilled-water isolation valves if active leak suspected
Check adjacent FCUs on same drain line
forbidden_actions: Assuming condensate without visual inspection
Leaving FCU valves open overnight pending repair if active leak
Working above live tenant workstations without clearing the area

exceptions.note: Drip onto tenant IT/electrical equipment — TS-01 electrical gate applies

rule_candidates.title: Fire-protection impairment requires FSM authorisation and red-tag
rule_candidates.decision: FSM (or deputy) authorises the impairment. Raise a red-tag impairment permit. Notify property insurer. Post fire watch patrols every 30 minutes in the affected zone. Restore protection as the first priority after life safety. Isolate the smallest sprinkler zone possible.
forbidden_actions: Technician closing a sprinkler control valve on own authority
Leaving the system impaired overnight without fire watch and FSM sign-off
Restoring protection without contractor functional test

rule_candidates.title: Lift pit water — take lift out of service and call contractor
rule_candidates.decision: Park lift at an upper floor and take out of service via FCC. Call lift maintenance contractor. Assess against BCA Reportable Matters Regulations 2025 — call BCA within 6 hours if a reportable safety incident occurred. Return to service only after contractor inspection and clearance.
allowed_actions: Take lift out of service via FCC
BCA incident call if reportable safety incident
forbidden_actions: Running the lift to 'test' with water in the pit
Entering the pit without contractor and isolation
Returning lift to service without contractor clearance

rule_candidates.title: No re-energisation without LEW sign-off
rule_candidates.decision: Re-energise affected AHU, DB, or circuit only after LEW inspection and certification. LEW inspects, tests insulation resistance, documents fitness. Technical Services restores in sequence. FCC confirms alarms normal. No re-energisation on visual inspection alone.
forbidden_actions: Re-energise before LEW sign-off
Re-energise on visual inspection alone
Re-energise before the room is dry
Reset a tripped breaker before LEW tests insulation resistance

exceptions.note: Critical facilities manager co-signs the LEW sign-off before return to service; the client SLA notice goes via the CFM (TS-10, TE-06)

rule_candidates.threshold_note: The 2 m proximity threshold (water_near_electrical) is the expert's professional judgement, not a code requirement (00:16:30, 00:25:00).

rule_candidates.title: Preserve evidence and photos for insurer before cleanup
rule_candidates.decision: Notify insurer or broker within the policy notification window. Preserve evidence: pre-cleanup photos with timestamps, failed component retained and tagged. Schedule loss adjuster. Separate landlord vs tenant damage scope. Do not commit to repairs beyond emergency mitigation before adjuster contact.
forbidden_actions: Disposing of the failed component before adjuster release
Committing to repairs beyond emergency mitigation before adjuster contact
Allowing cleanup before pre-cleanup photos are taken

rule_candidates.title: Start extraction and drying within 24 hours, verify dry within 48
rule_candidates.decision: Mobilise extraction, dehumidifiers and air movers. Moisture-map the affected area. Discard porous materials (ceiling tiles, fibreglass insulation). Re-check moisture at 24 hours and 48 hours. Drying equipment must be energised from circuits cleared by LEW, not from the affected board.
forbidden_actions: Closing up ceilings or walls before moisture readings are within target
Running drying equipment from circuits not yet cleared by LEW
Reusing wet porous materials

exceptions.note: Category 2/3 water — disinfect before drying; PPE required

rule_candidates.title: Data-centre CRAH or chilled-water leak — contain, escalate to CFM
rule_candidates.decision: Notify DC operations and critical facilities manager immediately. Isolate the water source (CRAC/CRAH condensate, chilled-water branch). Deploy containment and drip diversion. Any IT power-down is proposed only and executed by the IT/BCP owner or critical facilities manager. Client SLA notification is triggered via the critical facilities manager, not via the tenant experience comms flow.
allowed_actions: Notify critical facilities manager with evidence pack
Client SLA notification via critical facilities manager
forbidden_actions: Switching off IT racks or UPS output without BCP owner approval
Pumping water with equipment powered from in-room circuits
Sending tenant-experience comms to DC clients (use SLA channel)

exceptions.note: Water contacting live IT equipment — TS-01 electrical gate applies

rule_candidates.title: Clear stagnant water within 24 hours — NEA vector control
rule_candidates.decision: Remove standing water within 24 hours. Where it cannot be removed, treat with larvicide via pest-control contractor and inspect daily until dry. Record in the vector-control log. NEA holds owners and occupiers liable for mosquito breeding.
forbidden_actions: Leaving pooled water over a weekend without treatment
Discharging water into storm drains without checking for contaminants

rule_candidates.title: PUB heavy-rain alert — pre-emptive basement and roof checks
rule_candidates.decision: Within 30 minutes of the alert: test basement sump pumps and float switches, clear roof outlets and rainwater downpipes, stage flood barriers at carpark ramps and known low points, brief security on patrol points. Do not deploy barriers that block egress routes.
allowed_actions: Rainwater downpipe and roof drain clearance
Flood barrier deployment at carpark ramps
forbidden_actions: Deploying barriers that block egress routes
Ignoring a pump-run alarm during the warning window

rule_candidates.title: Emergency isolation before fire-protection red-tag — immediate life safety only
rule_candidates.decision: An immediate life-safety hazard (e.g. water on live equipment) is confirmed: isolate the fire-protection source first, inform the FSM within 5 minutes, and raise the red-tag impairment permit retrospectively. Fire watch, insurer notice and restoration then follow TS-05. This is the only path to a fire-protection isolation before FSM authorisation, and it holds only while the hazard is confirmed.
allowed_actions: Emergency isolation of the smallest zone that removes the hazard
Raise the red-tag impairment permit retrospectively
Post fire watch once the zone is isolated
forbidden_actions: Emergency isolation on an unconfirmed life-safety hazard
Isolating more than the zone needed to remove the hazard
Leaving the FSM uninformed beyond 5 minutes
Skipping the retrospective red-tag permit
